page: Microsoft Azure E8as_v6 is an Eav6-family virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor features a 32 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 vector extensions, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and SHA cryptography extensions. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the E8as_v6 demonstrates strong single-core performance, placing in the top 25% for both stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core scores. Text processing performance is exceptionally high, ranking in the top 10% of Geekbench text processing results. Multi-core performance and memory write bandwidth fall within the average range. However, a notable performance tradeoff exists in memory read bandwidth for large, potentially uncached blocks, which registers in the bottom 25%. Similarly, prompt processing for medium-sized language models is relatively weak, also scoring in the bottom 25%.

From a resource density perspective, the E8as_v6 offers a high memory allocation relative to its compute footprint, making it a cost-efficient option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The absence of local storage means storage costs are decoupled, relying on external Premium Storage. Given its high single-core speed, top-tier text processing, and substantial memory capacity, this instance is suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, text-heavy processing pipelines, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
